quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the best way to handle tailgaters?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes when you can and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: Which color is best to wear so others can see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding. Bright clothing helps drivers see you at any time of day.

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing gloves?

options.text: Make it difficult to control a motorcycle and should be avoided.
Provide a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What should you do when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride as you would without a passenger.
Make sure footrests are available only for you.
Tell the passenger what to do after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be equipped and adjusted for a passenger. It needs a separate seat, footrests for the passenger, and may need adjustments to the headlight, tire pressure, and suspension to handle the extra weight.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to handle differently?

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over to check the chain.
Pull over to check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A change in handling may mean a tire has failed. Pull over safely and check your tires if you notice a change in how your motorcycle handles.

questions.question: When should you wear a jacket while riding?

options.text: No matter what the weather is.
Only if you will ride for more than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter what the weather is.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. A jacket protects you from the sun and dehydration in hot weather.

questions.question: How often should you do a complete check of your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: What reduces head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection against injury in a crash.

questions.question: What material offers the best protection for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather clothing provides the best protection for motorcyclists. Wear clothing that covers your legs and arms completely when riding.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car, what happens?

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car. Drivers check their rearview mirror much more often than their side mirror. This position makes it more likely the driver will see you.

questions.question: When braking, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time to stop. The brakes work best when you use them together.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of for the best protection?
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong material to protect your hands.

questions.question: What should your clothing do when you ride a motorcycle?

options.text: Be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Not cover your arms or legs completely.
Not include a jacket in warm weather.

questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you if you crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothes should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind but should be loose enough for you to move freely.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane.

questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, oil, and metal plates are all slippery. Dry pavement gives your tires the best grip.

questions.question: How should you check your tire pressure?

options.text: Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Check your tire pressure with a tire gauge before every ride. A visual check is not reliable because an under-inflated tire can still look normal.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes if you can do so safely. Riding faster can make things more dangerous because the tailgater may just follow at the higher speed.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is securely fastened is the single best thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: What should you do about mirror checks?

options.text: Do them only on long trips.
Make them part of your normal scanning routine.
They are not helpful because you cannot do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal riding routine. Also check them before changing lanes, before stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle operator be ready for when passing parked cars?

options.text: A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
Other drivers seeing your motorcycle and staying out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull out into traffic. It is safest to ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you the most space between your motorcycle and any dangers.

questions.question: What should a rider do to prevent fatigue on long rides?

options.text: Complete the ride with as few stops as possible.
Use caffeine or other artificial stimulants.
Travel as far as possible in one day.

questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from heat, rain, wind, and snow. Ride no more than six hours per day. Stop to rest at least every two hours. Do not use caffeine or stimulants. When they wear off, you may feel extreme fatigue.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps you be seen in any condition. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing at all times.

questions.question: What should you do while riding?

options.text: Look ahead and anticipate potential hazards.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards since they are minimal on roads.
Look ahead but avoid looking for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and anticipate potential hazards.
questions.explanation: Always look ahead down the road. This helps you see hazards early and react to them before you reach them.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Turn it on only if it is cloudy.
Turn it on only if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a bridge grating?

options.text: Ride on the far right side of the lane.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is usually not dangerous. Stay calm and ride straight across at a steady speed. Do not zigzag, as this forces you to swerve across your lane and is dangerous.
